name: Duchy of Cleves
alt: Duchy of Cleves and County of Mark

predecessors.name: Duchy of Lower Lorraine
predecessors.text: the County of Cleves: 'The first documented lord from the House of Cleves is Dietrich ... in 1092'

successors.name: Electorate of Brandenburg
successors.text: 'Brandenburg received Cleves-Mark and Neuburg received Jülich-Berg' (Treaty of Xanten, 12 November 1614; infobox 'To Brandenburg: 1614') (Soest included, held since 1449)

ledger.x: 1391: Mark. 'In 1391, Adolph III also inherited the Mark from his elder brother Engelbert III'; the Mark page says he 'united both counties as Cleves-Mark in 1394'. The Cleves page puts the personal union after Engelbert III died without issue in 1391.
1417: King Sigismund 'raised Count Adolph I to the status of a duke and a Prince of the Holy Roman Empire in 1417', and the county became a duchy.

5 June 1444: Soest rejects Archbishop Dietrich of Cologne by 'accepting a new suzerain, John I of Cleves-Mark, the Duke of Cleves-Mark', who guaranteed the town its old rights; the feud runs 'from 1444 to 1449'.
1449: the Soest Feud ends; the page's bibliography dates its end to 27 April of the year (the anniversary 'Beendigung der Soester Fehde am 27.
12 November 1614: 'Eventually, the Treaty of Xanten was approved on 12 November 1614.'

wars.name: Soest Feud
wars.outcome: Soest, an enclave in Cologne's land, takes John I of Cleves-Mark as suzerain on 5 June 1444 and stays with the Duchy of Cleves after the feud ends in 1449 (the Feud page gives no treaty; its bibliography implies 27 April 1449).

wars.name: War of the Jülich Succession (Cleves-Mark)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Xanten (12 November 1614) gave Cleves-Mark and Ravensberg to Brandenburg; the Dutch held Cleves and Mark and the Spanish took Wesel in 1614.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and dukes, not boundaries; the only area is 'approximately 3,000 km2' for the Mark.
